unit.why: The division finishes the Radoshitz rebbe's deathbed-confession anecdote from the previous division, then gives a second tale: the Radoshitz rebbe's habitual story about R. Hayyim Haikl of Amdur, followed by a short homiletic coda on semikha.
unit.boundary_note: first story begins in previous division (Tiferet-Hayyim_0021)

stories.start_quote: לעבוד להשי"ת יותר בשקידה זה ג״כ
stories.summary_en: During an illness the Radoshitz rebbe reasons that he cannot honestly confess sins or laxity, so he resolves instead to serve God with purer intent if healed; he recovers and lives about twenty more years.

quotes: וכן הי׳ שנתרפא מחליו וחי עוד לערך עשרים שנה
tags.why: recovery from illness follows his resolution
recovery implied as answer to his vow

quotes: לעבוד להשי"ת בדעת צלולה וזכה בלי שום פניה
tags.why: sincerity and pure service of God
illustrates the tzaddik's truthfulness and devotion

quotes: רק זאת אוכל לקבל עלי מהיום והלאה
tags.why: deathbed confession and resolution, framed as viduy

stories.start_quote: וכמו ששמענו מאת הה״ק מראדשיץ זלה"ה
stories.summary_en: The Radoshitz rebbe often told how R. Hayyim Haikl of Amdur fasted from Sabbath to Sabbath and kept a thousand night vigils of study, yet his tikkun was completed only when he came to the Maggid of Mezeritch for a Sabbath; the text then explains this as the power of semikha passed from Moses to Joshua.

quotes: שעשה בעצמו כמה סגופי׳ להתענות משבת לשבת
ואלף לילות ה׳ ניעור משנתו ללמוד כל הלילה
עד אשר בא לרבינו הקדוש מוהד״ב ממעזריטש זלה"ה על שבת
tags.why: comes to the Maggid for Sabbath
the decisive visit is a Sabbath

quotes: וזה הענין כח הסמיכה ביד הצדיקים
tags.why: only the tzaddik can complete a person's tikkun

quotes: ועכ״ז לא נגמר תיקונו עד אשר בא
tags.why: his soul's tikkun is completed through the Maggid
R. Hayyim Haikl becomes the Maggid's disciple
the Radoshitz rebbe habitually told this tale

quotes: כמ״ש ויהושע בן נון מלא רוח חכמה
tags.why: exegesis of a verse on semikha
anecdote cited inside a homiletic frame from Tiferet Shlomo

missing_concepts: semikha / transmission of spirit from master to disciple
limits of self-perfection without a master
